correctness.rationale: Edge transitivity plus complete ordered-pair third-neighbor profiles gives three-round equivalence; line-graph common-neighbor counts are d-2+ε on adjacent pairs and at most four on nonadjacent pairs, with both exclusive neighbor types present. For n≥5, binom(n,k)≥10 ensures a third edge avoiding up to four endpoints; the octahedron has both exceptional leftover-edge outcomes. Johnson graphs J(4,2),J(5,2) have no induced 2K2 because each original adjacent pair uses three K_n atoms, and n<6 forbids two disjoint supports. Explicit induced 2K2 examples inside J(6,2) or J(6,3) extend to all n≥6. Two rank-three separator sentences yield necessity. Two independent finite checkers replay complete signatures and game types.

value.rationale: A complete and sharp classification of a natural two-parameter family of edge-adjacency graphs, where both ambient n and subset size k are unbounded. The exact induced-matching transition at six ground elements identifies which graph property rank-three logic first detects, while the 60-vertex sharp representative shows that substantially larger and higher-dimensional line graphs collapse to one bounded-depth theory. Not simply a small finite computation or a restatement of the known base Johnson graph classifications.
